# WaveShift

> WaveShift is a browser-based audio conversion website. Visitors can select audio files, choose an output format, convert files in their browser, and download the results.

WaveShift is designed for people who need straightforward audio format conversion and WAV compression. The website is written in English and is intended for a worldwide audience.

## Main tools

- [Online Audio Converter](https://your-netlify-site.netlify.app/): Convert supported audio files to MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG or M4A in a browser.
- [MP3 to WAV Converter](https://your-netlify-site.netlify.app/mp3-to-wav.html): Create a WAV version of an MP3 for editing or software that requires WAV.
- [WAV to MP3 Converter](https://your-netlify-site.netlify.app/wav-to-mp3.html): Convert WAV audio to MP3 and select an output bitrate.
- [WAV Compressor](https://your-netlify-site.netlify.app/wav-compressor.html): Create a smaller MP3 copy or a lossless FLAC copy from a WAV file.

## Supported formats and workflow

- Output formats offered by the main converter: MP3, WAV, FLAC, OGG, and M4A.
- The file picker accepts common audio extensions including MP3, WAV, M4A, AAC, FLAC, OGG, OGA, OPUS, WMA, AIFF, and AIF. Actual support depends on the codec contained in the file.
- Multiple files can be selected. The website processes them sequentially and provides a separate download for each converted file.
- MP3 and M4A output offers bitrate choices of 128, 192, 256, and 320 kbps.
- WAV compression offers MP3 for smaller lossy output or FLAC for lossless compression.

## Privacy and technical notes

- Audio conversion runs in the visitor's browser. The website does not provide a WaveShift audio-upload endpoint or server-side audio storage.
- The browser downloads the FFmpeg WebAssembly conversion engine from a public CDN when conversion is first used. This is separate from uploading the visitor's audio file.
- Large audio files may use significant browser memory and device resources. Conversion speed depends on the visitor's device, browser, file length, and codec.
- Converting a lossy file to WAV does not restore audio information removed by an earlier lossy encode.
- The website does not claim that format conversion improves the source recording's sound quality.
